summary: This Dockerfile creates a Ubuntu container with zsh shell fully configured. It installs zsh along with essential tools like git and curl, then layers in Oh-My-Zsh (a zsh configuration framework), adds syntax highlighting as a plugin, customizes the shell prompt with a container emoji, and sets zsh as the default interactive login shell when the container starts.

explanations.3: This prevents apt-get from pausing to ask interactive questions during installation, which would hang the Docker build process.
explanations.5: The && operator chains these commands together so if any step fails, the whole RUN instruction fails, preventing a broken image from being created.
explanations.11: After installing packages, this deletes the package cache files to reduce the final image size, since we won't need to re-download packages.
explanations.14: This downloads and runs the Oh-My-Zsh installation script from GitHub, the --unattended flag makes it skip interactive prompts, and --keep-zshrc prevents it from overwriting any existing zsh config.
explanations.18: The --depth=1 flag tells git to only download the latest commit, not the entire history, which saves space in the image.
explanations.20: The sed command finds the line starting with 'plugins=(git)' and replaces it with one that includes zsh-syntax-highlighting, which adds colored syntax highlighting to typed commands.
explanations.25: The -i flag makes zsh interactive and -l makes it a login shell, so it loads your full shell configuration including aliases and environment variables when the container starts.
